response: Do not force-shutdown your PC yet. A force-shutdown during an update can corrupt system files and make Windows unbootable. Start with the safest step: wait another hour. Large updates can genuinely take this long on slower hardware. If it is still stuck after that, try pressing Ctrl+Alt+Del to see if the system responds. If it does, restart normally from that screen. If the system is completely frozen, a force-restart may be unavoidable, but first try holding the power button for 10 seconds only as a last resort. After restarting, run the Windows Update troubleshooter: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Windows Update. If problems persist, you can try Disk Cleanup as administrator to free space, or use System Restore to roll back before the update. One step at a time.
action_plan: Warn against force-shutdown as the first option.
Try Ctrl+Alt+Del for a clean restart.
Run the Windows Update troubleshooter after restart.
Offer progressive escalation: Disk Cleanup, System Restore, safe mode.
principles_used: Start with the safest reversible step.
Explain the risk of force-shutdown during updates.
Give one step at a time to avoid overwhelming the user.
